title: Gap-Up fades as IT and HDFC Bank drag Nifty to near-flat; crude, Rupee weigh - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Benchmark indices surrendered the bulk of their early gains by mid-session on Monday, October 5, 2026, as selling pressure in IT heavyweights and HDFC Bank offset strength in financials and consumer stocks. The Nifty 50 was at 22,451.60, up just 29.65 points or 0.13 per cent, at 12.25 pm, while the Sensex stood at 71,982.16, a gain of 72.46 points or 0.10 per cent, sharply paring a gap-up opening that had sent the indices more than 150 points higher at the bell.

Bank Nifty, which had surged over 600 points in early trade, surrendered nearly all its gains through the session. Among sectoral indices, Nifty Consumer Durables was the best performer while Nifty Pharma was the worst. Broader market breadth turned negative: on BSE, 2,365 stocks declined against 1,889 advances, with 163 stocks hitting 52-week lows against 127 at 52-week highs. A total of 246 stocks were locked in lower circuits, outnumbering the 178 in upper circuits.

TMPV led Nifty 50 gainers with a 3.40 per cent rise to ₹288.90, followed by Bajaj Finance, which added 2.81 per cent to ₹974.95. BSE Ltd gained 2.46 per cent to ₹3,120.90, Shriram Finance rose 2.37 per cent to ₹967.35, and ITC advanced 2.34 per cent to ₹261.90. PSU banks and the broader financial sector continued to provide the primary support for the market.

On the losing side, HCL Technologies fell 3.39 per cent to ₹1,200.90, leading declines among IT stocks even as Accenture’s strong quarterly results had been expected to lift the sector. Asian Paints slid 2.67 per cent to ₹2,342.80. HDFC Bank, which had drawn buyers in the morning session after a strong provisional second-quarter business update, reversed course to trade 2.55 per cent lower at ₹702.80 — among the most heavily traded stocks on the exchange with a transaction value of ₹3,14,457.20 lakh. Infosys dropped 2.26 per cent to ₹1,011.60, and HDFC Life slipped 1.42 per cent to ₹526.60.

Sudeep Shah, Vice President, Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, noted that “...meaningful call writing witnessed across 22,500 and 22,600 strikes,” while the put side showed substantial open interest at 22,400 and 22,300. The Nifty’s advance-decline ratio stood at 30:20. Shah placed immediate Nifty support at 22,320–22,340 and resistance at 22,630–22,650, with the Sensex supported at 71,600 and resistance at 72,500.

Commodity markets added further caution. MCX Crude Oil opened with a sharp gap-down and was trading 2.71 per cent lower, while WTI Crude declined 1.40 per cent to near $90 a barrel. MCX Gold fell 0.67 per cent to around ₹149,000 after opening at ₹151,197, while MCX Silver outperformed, trading near ₹227,000, up 0.39 per cent. COMEX Silver was up 1.90 per cent to near $61.50, sharply outperforming COMEX Gold, which was up a marginal 0.22 per cent near $4,170.

The Indian rupee remained under pressure, trading near ₹96.20 to the dollar. Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, noted that “...persistent rupee weakness remains a key concern for domestic markets, particularly given the impact of elevated energy prices on India’s import bill and inflation outlook.”

Markets will now watch for further directional cues ahead of the RBI Monetary Policy Committee decision on October 7, where a 25-basis-point rate hike is widely expected.
